title: Police board diversity plan and affordable housing approvals
subtitle: Also: Westmount Road design, bridge and road expropriations, transit requests, measles update, CAO hiring authority.
overview: Regional Council adopted a 2025 diversity plan for the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board {{vote:m6}}, keeping the board at seven members. The provincial Community Safety and Policing Act requires the plan by April 1. Staff will return before the 2026 appointments with public engagement strategies, and the Regional Chair will write to the province about the skills expected of its appointees.

Council also approved a revised five-year affordable housing framework and a federal loan agreement for the Waterloo Region Housing building at 589 Langs Drive in Cambridge {{vote:m3}}. It approved a design for Westmount Road in Kitchener, expropriations for the Scheifele Bridge replacement and Lancaster Street West improvements, and a U-turn prohibition on Charles Street {{vote:m4}}. A closed committee recommendation updated CAO hiring authority and supported a co-operative housing proposal {{vote:m5}}.

Delegates asked for a seniors' transit fare, bus service to a Hindu temple, an end to the Wilmot land assembly and a settlement with striking CUPE 1656 workers. Council asked staff to report on pilot days of temple service. The medical officer of health said no measles cases have been found in the region, and that school suspensions for incomplete immunization records begin April 2.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the 2025 Municipal Diversity Plan for the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board, kept the board at seven members, and directed staff to return with an updated plan and the Chair to write to the province.

decisions.item: Affordable housing framework and Langs Drive loan
decisions.detail: Council approved the revised Building Better Futures Framework for 2025 to 2030, contingent on federal and provincial funding, and authorized a CMHC loan agreement for the 589 Langs Drive affordable housing building in Cambridge.

Council approved the Westmount Road design alternative, endorsed water operational plans and the 2024 drinking water report, approved expropriations for the Scheifele Bridge replacement and Lancaster Street West, and added a U-turn prohibition on Charles Street at Cedar Street.

Council amended the signing authority and CAO by-laws to give the CAO authority over department head hiring and structure recommendations, and authorized a conditional six-month letter of commitment for a co-operative housing lease proposal.

debate: A delegate argued that Grand River Transit should offer seniors a discounted fare, possibly as a pilot, citing lower fares elsewhere and saying proving need is demeaning. Staff replied that GRT has moved to need-based discounts through the affordable transit program, and that seniors' fares will be covered in the business plan going to committee on April 8.

A temple representative asked for GRT service to the temple, saying seniors without vehicles cannot reach it and that large events bring heavy car traffic. Staff said weekend service with a closer stop would cost about $720,000 a year and was not in the 2025 plan, but offered to explore pilot days. Councillors asked for a report with options and financial implications.
A delegate opposed the Wilmot land assembly, saying it cuts into the countryside line, threatens high-quality farmland during tariff concerns, and has damaged trust. Council asked no questions.
A labour council delegate urged council to meet the demands of striking CUPE 1656 workers and called for support for Palestinians. Council asked no questions.

On the police board plan, councillors asked for accessibility to be reflected by using the READI acronym, and one raised concern that a single appointee could be tokenized. Staff said expanding to nine would add a provincial appointee and a regional councillor, which the Region does not control, so they proposed advocacy to the province. Councillors also suggested advocating for more community representatives.
